preceding_messages.speaker: Y
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the shared-lineage gate and its suppressed-cell output verbatim; it converts a vendor-family or cadence-mismatch artifact into an explicitly inconclusive record that a year-three reader can parse as structurally unvalidated rather than as a failed comparison. The concrete design choice I advance: whenever the lineage gate passes and a numeric delta does print, the cell must simultaneously carry an uncertainty band equal to the root-sum-square of both sites' residual calibration uncertainties at the shared-event instant plus a fixed structural term of 0.3 mm/h for residual cadence-aliasing, and if the band's half-width meets or exceeds the delta magnitude the cell appends "— Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY," so the comparison reports a number flagged as statistically indistinguishable from zero. The failure this qualifier closes: week 22, Site 7 (tipping-bucket, residual cal 0.8 mm/h) and Site 8 (rain gauge, residual cal 0.7 mm/h) jointly confirm the same cell thunderstorm and the comparison cell prints "0.9 mm/h," a neighborhood drainage-planning meeting reads the figure as Site 7 being meaningfully wetter, and a catch-basin upsizing is scoped for Site 7's culvert based on a divergence whose true identity is the sum of two calibration residuals masking zero spatial signal. With the appended band the cell reads "0.9 mm/h ± 1.06 mm/h — Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY," the drainage-planning committee correctly treats the divergence as unresolvable, defers the upsizing decision to the next confirmed shared event with tighter calibrations, and the record retains both the number and its nullification so the uncertainty budget is auditable rather than silently discarded.

preceding_messages.speaker: X
preceding_messages.text: I adopt the RSQ uncertainty band, the fixed 0.3 mm/h structural term, and the "Δ WITHIN UNCERTAINTY" qualifier verbatim; they convert a vendor-family offset into an explicitly nullified number the drainage-planning committee can read and defer. Because the band's inputs are residual calibration uncertainties that creep between certificate renewals, I mandate that any comparison cell whose residual was last renewed more than fourteen days before the shared-event instant expands the printed band by (trailing-30-day drift-slope × days-since-renewal) and appends "STALE CAL — BAND EXPANDED [+N d × slope]" alongside the base figure. The failure this closes: Site 7's week-10 delta of 1.2 mm/h exceeds the stale week-4 band of 1.06 mm/h and prints as a resolvable divergence, scoping a catch-basin upsizing against Site 7's culvert, while the true band incorporating six weeks of 0.04 mm/h/week creep computes to 1.31 mm/h and nullifies the divergence entirely. The staleness annotation, carrying the slope value and the renewal-date gap, lets a year-three appendix reader reconstruct that the "resolvable" figure was an artifact of delayed metrology service rather than a validated spatial signal, preserving the uncertainty budget's auditability without silently discarding the nullification.

target.speaker: Y
target.text: I adopt the trailing-30-day drift-slope expansion and the "STALE CAL — BAND EXPANDED" annotation verbatim; they make the nullification auditable to the metrology-service delay rather than to the spatial signal. Because a trailing-30-day slope estimate is itself vulnerable to short-duration environmental stress, I mandate that the operative slope be computed over a rolling 90-day window and that any divergence between the 30-day and 90-day slopes exceeding 50 % triggers the larger (conservative) slope with an appended "SLOPE DISAGREEMENT — CONSERVATIVE EXPANSION APPLIED" tag carrying both slope values and their respective window dates. The failure this closes: Site 8's two-week hail-event series mechanically stressed the gauge tip, inflating the 30-day slope to +0.12 mm/h/week against a true 90-day slope of +0.03 mm/h/week, and the over-expanded band nullifies a genuine 1.5 mm/h week-14 structural offset arising from Site 8's drainage-adjacent placement, deferring a legitimate culvert-sizing correction through another month of decaying hail-stress artifact. I therefore require that the conservative-slope annotation permits a year-three appendix reader to reconstruct the hail-stress transient and the underlying structural offset as independent causal variables rather than to read a single inflated number that conflates both.
